column1: # The pointer-order parity ceiling, enumerated per (member, observable)
# (cgz-r13, given a portable home by cgz-r26).
# Columns are tab separated:
#   member  observable  order_ceiling_bl  input_sha256  evidence
# member          `{partition}/{index}`, the corpus identity. Portable: every
#                 member is generated from nothing but those two values by an
#                 integer-only, value-pinned PRNG, so it does not move under a
#                 toolchain bump, an optimize-mode change, or a different
#                 architecture. See src/conformance/corpus.zig.
# observable      A name from `comparison.Observable`. An observable whose
#                 normal tier is exact may never appear: structural
#                 observables stay exact on ceiling members too.
# order_ceiling_bl  `-`, or a deviation bound in bond lengths (one bond = 50
#                 units). `-` means the pair is excused from *exact*
#                 comparison and nothing else; it keeps its normal tier's
#                 tolerance T. A number replaces T for that one pair. Only
#                 `coordinates` may carry a number, because it is the only
#                 observable the classifier measures a per-member magnitude
#                 for; a number on any other would be invented. A bound at or
#                 above 1.0 is rejected by the loader: above that boundary a
#                 "tolerant" pass no longer means the layout matched.
# input_sha256    SHA-256 of the member's canonical dump
#                 (`corpus.writeMolecule`). A property of the member, so every
#                 row naming it must repeat the same value. It is what makes
#                 the identity checkable rather than assumed: if the generator
#                 is ever edited, the identity still parses but now names a
#                 different molecule, and this digest is what catches that.
# evidence        The bead that admitted the row.
# THIS FILE IS THE AUTHORITATIVE CEILING. conformance/parity_manifest.tsv also
# names these members, but it is a per-(architecture, toolchain, optimize-mode)
# artifact and a gate that reads it changes meaning per host.
# conformance/parity_expectations.tsv is portable but its schema is
# per-partition fractions, and a fraction permits N failures without saying
# which N. Neither can carry this enumeration; this file exists because both
# properties are required at once.
# Fail closed. A (member, observable) pair measured order-unstable with no row
# here is a hard failure, not a budget hit — `zig build corpus-check` enforces
# that, and `comparison.differentialComparison` returns
# error.UnenumeratedOrderInstability for it. The converse is not a failure: a
# row is permission, not obligation, so an enumerated pair that happens to be
# stable on some host passes.
# Admitting a member is a code review event with a recorded measurement, the
# same standing as regenerating the manifest. Add the row, cite the bead that
# measured it, and state the headroom in a comment above it so a later
# widening appears as a diff.
# With deterministic ascending and descending controls, the two CI targets
# measure ten transform members in their union. Transform-only differences are
# one to a few units in the last place. adversarial/680 and 811 additionally
# move coordinates on x86_64-linux, and adversarial/1538 moves coordinates on
# both targets; `-` keeps all three at the normal coordinate tolerance rather
# than inventing or widening a per-member bound. These rows consume the
# existing fraction ceilings (4 coordinate and 10 transform members) without
# widening them.

# 0.580 bond lengths under reversed heap address order. The bound is 0.75,
# which is 0.17 bond lengths of headroom over that measurement and 0.25 below
# the 1.0 boundary where a deviation stops being float jitter and becomes a
